4.title: Biography
4.content: Rauf Shah, MS, PhD is a Lead Health Data Coordinator II working at the intersection of clinical genomics, oncology bioinformatics, and public health. He designs secure, reproducible pipelines that link registries, EHR, digital pathology, and genomics via FHIR/HAPI to support cancer surveillance, ctDNA/lymphoma analytics, and equity-focused outcomes. As an MPH–Epidemiology student, his interests include timeliness and quality in cancer surveillance, situational awareness for disaster epidemiology, and the translation of data into decision-ready dashboards for clinicians and policy partners. He is also committed to public-health teaching and training, including the design of practice-oriented courses and modules in surveillance systems, FHIR data engineering, and reproducible analytics.

19.title: CPH 705 — Public Health Teaching and Training

20.title: Course Overview
20.content: CPH 705 PUBLIC HEALTH TEACHING AND TRAINING . This course is designed to develop graduate students’ teaching skills and strategies necessary to meet the professional demands of conducting public health teaching and training. Major topics covered include adult learning theory, instructional design, needs analysis, training program evaluation, and creating teaching modules for in-person, synchronous, and asynchronous environments.

Needs Assessment & Program Evaluation . | Systematic approaches to identifying training needs | Data collection methods for educational program planning | Evaluation frameworks for measuring training effectiveness | Continuous improvement cycles for educational programs | . 24.title: Course Reflections
24.content: CPH 705 provided foundational training in evidence-based teaching methodologies specifically tailored for public health education. The course emphasized the systematic design of learning experiences, from initial needs assessment through program evaluation, with particular focus on adapting teaching strategies for diverse public health audiences and delivery formats. The skills developed in this course directly support my commitment to public health teaching and training, including curriculum development for cancer surveillance, FHIR/HAPI training workshops, and reproducible analytics education. The backward design approach ensured alignment between public health competencies, learning objectives, and instructional activities, while the focus on multi-modal delivery prepared me to create accessible and effective learning experiences across different educational contexts. This training enhances my ability to develop practice-oriented public health education that bridges research and practice.
